package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to 5.3.18 and 5.2.20 (Java 9+ required)
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerability (CVE-2022-22965, 'SpringShell') allows remote attackers to manipulate internal ClassLoader attributes via crafted POST requests, enabling arbitrary file write and remote code execution (RCE) on affected Spring Web applications running on Java 9+ and Tomcat.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request to a Spring Web endpoint accepting POJOs)
execution_context.file_location: Any exposed Spring Web controller endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker sends a crafted POST request that manipulates Tomcat's logging configuration via Spring's data binding, causing Tomcat to write a new .jsp file containing attacker-controlled code to a web-accessible directory, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows external input to reconfigure server internals and write executable files, which is never expected from user input.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Spring Web applications should not allow POST parameters to alter ClassLoader or Tomcat context attributes, nor write arbitrary files to the web root.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate configuration changes are performed by administrators via secure channels, not by end-users via HTTP requests.
key_indicators: Modification of Tomcat pipeline attributes via HTTP input
Creation of .jsp files in web-accessible directories
Pattern parameter containing web shell or executable code

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request after malicious file creation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the malicious JSP file is written, the attacker sends an HTTP GET request to the new .jsp file, triggering execution of the embedded web shell code, which can execute arbitrary commands on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Execution of attacker-controlled code via a newly created web-accessible file is a classic remote code execution pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Web applications should not allow arbitrary file creation or execution of user-supplied code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JSP files are used for dynamic web content, but should only be deployed by trusted developers/admins.
key_indicators: Unexpected .jsp files appearing in web root
JSP code containing command execution logic
Access to new .jsp file immediately after suspicious POST

attack_chain.action: Attacker locates a POST endpoint in the Spring application that accepts POJOs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to send crafted POST requests to manipulate internal server attributes.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted POST request with class.module.classLoader.* parameters to reconfigure Tomcat logging to write a .jsp file containing malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary file write of a malicious JSP web shell to a web-accessible directory.

attack_chain.action: Attacker triggers a logging event (or relies on normal logging) to ensure the malicious code is written to the new .jsp file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JSP file is now present on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses the new .jsp file via HTTP GET, executing the embedded web shell code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the server (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: POST requests with parameters prefixed by class.module.classLoader.*
Unexpected changes to Tomcat logging configuration at runtime
Creation of new .jsp files in web-accessible directories
Execution of newly created .jsp files containing web shell code
file_indicators: webapps/ROOT/ohno.jsp (or other unexpected .jsp files in web root)
JSP files containing suspicious code patterns (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec)
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests to Spring endpoints with class.module.classLoader.* parameters
Subsequent GET requests to new .jsp files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing class.module.classLoader.* parameters, especially those targeting Spring Web endpoints. Alert on creation of new .jsp files in web-accessible directories and on execution of JSP files not present in the original deployment. Review Tomcat configuration changes at runtime and scan for JSP files containing suspicious code patterns (e.g., command execution).
